at_commands.source_scope_note: The supplied module hardware-design document names the separate “SIM808 Series AT Command Manual” as related document [1] (physical page 66), but that manual is not supplied here. A family-level command catalog/manual is therefore not proof that any particular command is supported by this model or revision; only the module-document statements below are model-specific evidence.

module_specific_features.feature: AT+CBAND can set the four GSM/GPRS frequency bands.
AT+CPOWD=1 is identified as a normal power-off method.
AT+IPR=x can set and save a fixed baud rate.
AT+CFUN=<fun> controls functionality modes; the documented values are 0 minimum functionality, 1 full functionality (default), and 4 flight mode.
AT+echarge=1 enables the charging function, which is not supported by default.
AT+IFC=2,2 enables and AT+IFC=0,0 disables hardware flow control.
AT+CMIC adjusts microphone input gain; AT+SIDET sets side-tone level; AT+CLVL adjusts output gain.
AT+CSDT enables or disables SIM-card detection.
AT+SGPIO sets GPIO output voltage and reads GPIO input voltage.
AT + SPWM sets PWM output period and duty cycle; spacing is preserved from the extracted text.
Table 34 lists AT+CGNSPWR, AT+CGNSSEQ, AT+CGNSINF, AT+CGNSURC, AT+CGNSCMD and AT+CGNSTST for GNSS functions.
The GNSS prose states AT+CGNSSPWR=1 powers on and AT+CGNSSPWR=0 powers down GNSS; this spelling differs from Table 34 and is retained verbatim.

Bluetooth is described as having AT interfaces for pairing, bonding, pushing/receiving files, SPP service, and Bluetooth-headset-role remote-phone control; individual Bluetooth command names are not given in this document.

pcb_considerations.assertion: Power traces from VBAT to the supply must be at least 80mil wide; the power IC and bypass capacitor should be as close to the module as possible.

For antenna/RF layout: keep the conducted-test RF connector close to GSM_ANT, place matching close to the antenna, control RF traces to 50Ω, and keep them away from high-speed signals and strong disturbing sources.
If RF cable is used, keep it away from the SIM card and power ICs; place GSM and Bluetooth antennas as far apart as possible.

VBAT positive routing should be short and wide; the prescribed flow from source to VBAT goes through the Zener diode then a large capacitor. Pins 1, 2 and 3 should have the shortest layout to the power-source ground.
The 15 middle GND pads enhance GND performance; do not route signals on their upper layer if possible.
Place the SIM holder far from antenna/RF cable and near the module; add ESD protection to clock, data, reset and SIM_VDD, and keep these signals away from power and high-speed-frequency signals.
Audio traces should be surrounded by ground, kept away from antenna and power, and not routed parallel to VBAT.
UART signal lines should be routed bunched, as should USB and I2C signals.
USB_DP and USB_DN should be routed as differential traces.
Audio signals are to follow differential signal-layout rules.

antenna_requirements.assertion: SIM808 has GSM_ANT, BT_ANT and GPS_ANT; all antenna-port RF interfaces have 50Ω impedance.
Antenna input impedance should be 50Ω and VSWR should be less than 2; application-board antenna traces should be 50Ω controlled impedance.
Place the three antennas far apart; isolation among them should exceed 30dB.
GSM antenna connection must be DC-decoupled because the connector is DC-coupled to ground via an inductor for ESD protection; proper external antenna matching is necessary.
GSM matching values depend on antenna debug; normally R101 is 0Ω and C101/C102 are not mounted.
Bluetooth matching values depend on antenna debug; normally R201 is 0Ω and C201/C202 are not mounted.
GNSS can use passive or active antennas; selection is based on product design and other conditions, and proper matching is necessary.
For GNSS passive matching, component values can only be obtained after antenna tuning; normally R101 is 0Ω and C101/C102 are not mounted.
For an active GNSS antenna, VCC_ANT is required on the application board; L101 prevents RF leakage into the VCC_ANT path and routes bias, with recommended value no less than 27nH.

protection_circuits.assertion: A 5.1V/500mW Zener diode is strongly recommended on VBAT to prevent surge damage; it and the capacitors should be close to VBAT pins.
SIM signals should be protected against ESD with a TVS diode array; the SIM-card section recommends an ESD protection component such as ON SMF12CT1G.
SIM-card TVS parasitic capacitance should not exceed 50pF.
Maximum allowable TVS capacitive load on a USB data line should be less than 5pF; examples given are ESD9L5.0ST5G and ESD9M5.0ST5G.
A series RESET resistor can enhance ESD performance but must be less than 100Ω.
A keypad resistor less than 1KΩ can enhance keypad ESD performance.
For UART ESD consideration, the datasheet suggests 100ohm series resistances on UART lines.
In the active GNSS antenna circuit, R102 can protect the whole circuit if the active antenna is shorted to ground.
The speaker and microphone reference diagrams show ESD anti/ESD elements alongside the differential audio connections.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1 second and release; the power-on timing is illustrated.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: After power-on is complete, the module sends RDY to indicate it is ready to operate at fixed baud rate; the document says RDY does not appear until autobauding is active.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1.5 seconds and release; the timing is illustrated.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Before completion, the module sends NORMAL POWER DOWN; STATUS is low in power-off mode.

functional.method/procedure: With the GSM engine powered on and not in sleep mode, send AT+CGNSSPWR=1 as written in the GNSS operating-mode prose.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: The document states that, after power-on, the GNSS engine automatically acquires and tracks GNSS satellites.
The document states that the 1PPS pulse signal comes out after successful positioning.

functional.method/procedure: Table 2 gives performance values and notes conditions including 50% 24hr static at -130dBm, 50% at 30m/s, GNSS signal level -130dBm, and single 3.8V supply at -130dBm/GSM IDLE for power consumption.

communication.method/procedure: The document gives conducted output-power tables and states they follow 3GPP TS 05.05 technical-specification requirements.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: At GSM900/GSM850, output power should not exceed 33dBm, with maximum-level tolerance no more than ±2dB normal and ±2.5dB extreme; at DCS1800/PCS1900, it should not exceed 30dBm with the same respective maximum-level tolerances.

communication.method/procedure: The receive-sensitivity table is stated to be tested under static condition.
Table 3 reports receiver sensitivity for DH1 and DH5 at BER<0.1%, plus EDR receiver sensitivity for 2-DH5 and 3-DH5.

power.method/procedure: The illustrated test condition is VBAT=4.0V, CA=100µF tantalum (ESR=0.7Ω), and CB=1µF during maximum power transmit phase.
Table 42 is headed VBAT=4V with GNSS engine powered down and reports laboratory typical current values for the listed modes.
Apply the documented threshold conditions: ≤3.5V / ≥4.3V warning, and <3.4V / >4.4V power-down conditions.
power.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: The expected warnings are UNDER-VOLTAGE WARNNING or OVER-VOLTAGE WARNNING; below 3.4V or above 4.4V, the expected report is the respective POWER DOWN URC and automatic power-off.

environmental.method/procedure: The ESD table is stated at temperature 25℃ and humidity 45%, and reports contact- and air-discharge results by pin group.

missing_data.reason: The supplied source describes 68 SMT pads but does not explicitly declare a package type/name.

A separate SIM808 Series AT Command Manual is referenced but was not supplied; command references in the hardware document do not provide complete syntax, responses, or a revision-specific support matrix.

The source gives characterization data or conditions but no explicit pass/fail criteria for the records whose criteria are null (GNSS performance, receive sensitivity, Bluetooth sensitivity, VBAT drop, current consumption, and ESD).
Only version 1.03 of the SIM808 hardware-design source was supplied. The version-history change notes do not provide a second edition for direct fact-by-fact comparison.

ambiguities.issue: The text extraction contains no readable content of the Figure 2 pinout graphic; complete pinout records are consequently taken from Table 6 rather than inferred from the diagram.
The Figure 3 package-dimensions drawing exposes only its unit in the extracted text. The dimensions field uses the explicit “Size: 24*24*2.6mm” text rather than assigning drawing axes or tolerances.

On physical page 52, Table 34 spells the GNSS power command AT+CGNSPWR, while the operating-mode prose spells it AT+CGNSSPWR=1 and AT+CGNSSPWR=0. The source does not resolve whether this is a document typo or extraction issue; neither spelling was normalized.

The introductory overview describes “GPRS multi-slot class 12/ class 10 (optional),” while Table 1 says class 12 default and class 1–12 optional. Both explicit source statements are retained rather than reconciled.
GNSS Table 2 column alignment/labels are text-extraction-sensitive (the header reads “Min / Type / Max”); no Table-2 numerical-performance values are used as core technical-spec values in this JSON.
Physical page 55 refers to the active GNSS circuit as “Figure 54,” but its caption in the supplied text is Figure 49; the cited physical page is preserved.
The version-history page's footer displays printed page 8 although it is physical PDF page 9 after form-feed counting; all citations here use physical page numbers.
